title: We have released a demo of Shadows of the Fortificar. It is a D&D-based visual novel.
author: No_Application6041
selftext:
I’ve been developing the game Shadows of Fortificar for half a year now.

It’s a dark narrative RPG with elements of visual novels and strategy, based on D&D mechanics and inspired by games such as "Pathologic", "Baldur’s Gate", "The Life and Suffering of Sir Brante" and "The Banner Saga".

It is based on a real D&D campaign I ran as a Dungeon Master. Having left an indelible mark on my heart, it lingered in my mind for a long time, eventually taking shape as a video game that you can see here.

All of the game's art was generated using AI.



We recently released a demo on Itch.io!

I’d love for everyone to give it a try: [https://reddreamsstudio.itch.io/shadows-of-fortificar](https://reddreamsstudio.itch.io/shadows-of-fortificar)

comments.author: CocolitoCollective
comments.body: The art is really nice! Where did you make it? I’ll give it a try.

replies.author: No_Application6041
replies.body:
Thank you!

I hope you'll give it a try and share your thoughts - your feedback is really important to us right now!  


I work on the [openart.ai](http://openart.ai) website and use the Nano Banana Pro AI. It’s important to note that I run many generations, after which each selected image goes through a two-step processing - first by me (surface-level editing), then by my wife (she’s very skilled with graphic editors).

comments.author: Midnight-Magistrate
comments.body: The game looks great! Which engine did you use and what did you use to create the animations?

replies.author: No_Application6041
replies.body:
Thank you!

The game was built using the Unity engine. I have extensive experience working with it.

All the systems typical of visual novels were recreated by hand.

Most of the animations were created using DoTween.

By the way, here’s an interesting fact: the dice used for skill checks and its animations were all created by hand!

Be sure to give our game a try. We’d love to hear your thoughts on it.

comments.author: florodude
comments.body: Obviously this is just one little scene, but it's always really refreshing when posts on here have good effort and a consistent art style. Keep it up
